title: Lesson 89: Your Roadmap: The Next 90 Days of Learning and Building
description: Tests what each 30-day arc has to produce, where a rule that cannot have exceptions belongs, and the test that shows whether the workflow can be handed to somebody else.

questions.question: A ninety-day plan is organized as three 30-day arcs. What makes an arc a real unit of plan rather than a list of things to try?
options: It ends with a demonstration that impresses a reviewing room
It closes on one artifact and one number that can fail
It groups the tools you plan to try by how new they are
It names the frameworks you intend to evaluate carefully
questions.explanation: A roadmap is a dated sequence of artifacts, each with a number attached, so an arc is only real when it closes on something measurable that can fail. A list of tools or frameworks produces an opinion rather than a number.

questions.question: A rule must never be violated, no matter what the model decides on a given run. Where should that rule be enforced?
options: In the system prompt, restated at the start of every session
In the evaluation set, as a case that scores the behavior afterward
In hooks, deny rules and tests that run regardless of the model
In the design packet, so a later reviewer can confirm it existed
questions.explanation: An instruction the model reads is non-deterministic and can be declined on a given run, so it cannot carry a rule that must always hold. Rules with no exceptions belong in the harness, which executes hooks, deny rules and tests whether or not the model cooperates.

questions.question: A builder wants to know whether the workflow she built can keep producing numbers after she moves to another team. What test settles it?
options: The held-out split scores above the threshold written in the packet
The decision records list what was rejected as well as what was chosen
The evaluation suite runs on its own schedule whether or not anyone is watching
Somebody else runs the workflow for a week, with you reachable but not present
questions.explanation: The handoff test is whether a second person can operate the system while the builder is reachable but not present, which shows the work outlives its author. A plan with no handoff step was a personal project with a deadline.
